literal: Rare things having learned, fault those who are free from, even in, when examining, absence is rare indeed of ignorance.
translation: Even among those who have learned rare works and are free from faults, when examined closely, the complete absence of ignorance is rare indeed.
modern: அரிய நூல்களைக் கற்று, குற்றங்கள் இல்லாதவராக விளங்குபவர்களிடத்திலும் கூட, ஆராய்ந்து பார்க்கும் போது, அறியாமை இல்லாமல் இருப்பது என்பது மிகவும் அரிதானதே ஆகும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the realistic limits of human perfection, which is a vital lesson when choosing people for key duties. The poet explains that even when we look at highly learned individuals who seem entirely free of faults, a deep and close examination will still reveal some trace of ignorance. The word 'veḷiṟu' literally means whiteness or blankness, beautifully representing a blank spot of ignorance or folly in an otherwise brilliant mind. Therefore, expecting a complete absence of flaws in anyone is unrealistic, and one must learn to evaluate others by balancing their great merits against their minor shortcomings.
